::: {.bio}
I work on empirical asset pricing and financial econometrics. My research asks how the inputs to a characteristic-based factor model shape what the model tells us: the library of stock characteristics, the metric used to measure them, and the way estimated pricing errors are read. I follow these choices through identification and inference to the portfolios an investor ends up holding.

I received my PhD in Finance from Imperial College London in 2026, and I am a Visiting Researcher at the Imperial Centre of Excellence in Quantitative Finance. Before Imperial, I studied financial mathematics and economics at the University of Michigan and economics at Columbia University.
:::
:::

## Research

::: {.paper-cards}
::: {.pcard .jmp}
[[Job market paper]{.tag .jmp} Working paper · September 2026]{.pcard-meta}

### [Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions](/research/characteristic-libraries.html)

Repeating or rescaling existing stock characteristics can change a tuned investment rule without adding information.

[[Paper page](/research/characteristic-libraries.html) · [PDF](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Libraries_and_Portfolio_Decisions_SSRN_v2.pdf)]{.pcard-links}
:::

::: {.pcard}
[SSRN preprint · September 2026]{.pcard-meta}

### [Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html)

Factor models can fit returns identically yet split them differently among latent factors, observed factors and an intercept; an inner product on characteristic space selects the split.

[[Paper page](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html) · [PDF](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Space_Metrics_Main.pdf) · [SSRN](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7445120)]{.pcard-links}
:::

::: {.pcard}
[SSRN preprint · March 2026]{.pcard-meta}

### [A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models](/research/geometric-framework.html)

Identification depends on the metric that decides which directions in characteristic space are economically distinct, and the long-run cross-section of firm characteristics supplies that metric.

Earlier, broader version; the identification and inference results continue in [Characteristic-Space Metrics](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html) (above).

[[Paper page](/research/geometric-framework.html) · [PDF](/assets/pdfs/Geometric_Framework_SSRN_7013178.pdf) · [SSRN](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7013178)]{.pcard-links}
:::

::: {.pcard}
[Working paper · September 2026]{.pcard-meta}

### [Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice](/research/characteristic-geometry.html)

Nearly identical forecasts generate different portfolios because a fixed adjustment to factor variances imposes different exposure penalties across measurement conventions.

[[Paper page](/research/characteristic-geometry.html) · [Slides (PDF)](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Geometry_and_Portfolio_Choice_Slides.pdf)]{.pcard-links}
:::

::: {.pcard}
[Working paper · September 2026]{.pcard-meta}

### [Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts](/research/interpreting-pricing-errors.html)

When one model reports smaller estimated pricing errors, the paper separates changes in fitted expected returns from changes in factor loading spaces, and finds that a large gap mainly reflects different estimated means.

[[Paper page](/research/interpreting-pricing-errors.html) · [PDF](/assets/pdfs/Interpreting_Estimated_Pricing_Errors.pdf)]{.pcard-links}
:::
:::
